prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py only skipped JSON pre-parsing when a field's annotation was exactly `str`, so any union type containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`) still got run through json.loads(), silently corrupting string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. '{"a":1}' or 'null'). Both PRs replace the `annotation is not str` check with logic that also skips pre-parsing for union types whose non-str members can't come from JSON decoding. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py only skipped JSON pre-parsing when a field's annotation was exactly `str`, so any union type containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`) still got run through json.loads(), silently corrupting string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. '{"a":1}' or 'null'). Both PRs replace the `annotation is not str` check with logic that also skips pre-parsing for union types whose non-str members can't come from JSON decoding. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() before inspecting union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the common idiomatic pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None`. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() checks raw union args against a frozenset of bare types {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated-wrapped str member never matches the frozenset and _should_pre_parse_json still returns True - the corruption bug persists for any Optional[str] parameter that carries a Field/description via Annotated, which is a very common shape in practice. #3056's docstring also gives an explicit rationale for scoping the fix to str|None specifically (vs. e.g. str|list[str], where a member other than str could legitimately arise from JSON decoding), whereas #2032's broader 'skip for any union of scalar types' rule risks skipping legitimate int/float/bool coercion for unions like str|int or str|bool.

prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add rejection of an id already in flight, but #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids like int `1` and string "1" into the same key — a numeric id in flight would falsely reject a same-valued string id (or vice versa), and a string id equal to the literal "_GET_stream" could still collide with GET_STREAM_KEY. #3221 replaces this with a `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes by type (`i:`/`s:`), preserving the int/string distinction and structurally preventing collision with GET_STREAM_KEY, closing gaps #3063 leaves open while solving the same duplicate-id problem.

prs.author: ctaylor86
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock in async_auth_flow is held for the entire duration of `yield request` (i.e. across the full outbound request/response cycle), so any long-running or streaming request (e.g. a standalone SSE GET) blocks every other concurrent request on the same provider from acquiring the lock, closes #2847. (3 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3243 is the only one of the three that also addresses a correctness gap in the other two approaches: httpx can resume or close the async_auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that entered the `async with self.context.lock` block, which is unsafe with anyio.Lock's owner-task release semantics. #3243 replaces the single Lock with two task-agnostic anyio.Semaphore(1) locks (`lock` and `flow_lock`), separating token-acquisition serialization from the refresh/authorization transition. #3252's fix (move `yield request` outside the lock, re-acquire around the 401/403 branches) keeps the same Lock type and task-ownership assumption. #2858 is a rebase of an older, previously stalled PR (#2660); the diff available for it shows only import/docstring cleanup (the httpx2->httpx typo), not the actual lock-scope restructuring, so its concrete handling of the same-task-resumption issue is unverified.

prs.title: Fix OAuthClientProvider._initialize() to enable transparent token refresh
prs.author: draesthetic
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider loses track of stored-token expiry (and its refresh-endpoint metadata) across a process restart. `_initialize()` loads `current_tokens` from storage but never recomputes `token_expiry_time`, so `is_token_valid()` treats an already-expired restored token as valid, the proactive refresh branch never fires, and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization on the first request instead of silently refreshing. (4 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider loses track of stored-token expiry (and its refresh-endpoint metadata) across a process restart. `_initialize()` loads `current_tokens` from storage but never recomputes `token_expiry_time`, so `is_token_valid()` treats an already-expired restored token as valid, the proactive refresh branch never fires, and the client falls through to a full interactive re-authorization on the first request instead of silently refreshing. (4 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3251 contains the identical root-cause fix as #1784 (calling context.update_token_expiry() on the token loaded in _initialize()) and additionally restores oauth_metadata via a getattr/inspect-guarded duck-typed load, covering the goal of #2492 without requiring #2492's addition of get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata to the TokenStorage Protocol (a wider interface change downstream storage implementations would need to adopt). #1784 is a strict subset of #3251's _initialize change. #2875 patches the same bug from a different call site (the 401 handler in async_auth_flow) and its own inline comment attributes the need for that patch directly to _initialize never restoring token_expiry_time — once that's fixed at the source (as in #3251/#1784), #2875's fallback path is redundant.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (esp. UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ replays self.args through the subclass constructor, whose signature doesn't match (issue #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError subclasses (esp. UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ replays self.args through the subclass constructor, whose signature doesn't match (issue #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Diff base is c2a7fd44e7, a later revision than #2478/#2555's f153ea319d, so it applies cleanly against the more current file. It fixes __reduce__ on the base MCPError class using __new__ + Exception.__init__ plus a state dict, restoring the full __dict__ generically for any subclass instead of special-casing types. #2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError, leaving every other MCPError subclass (e.g. NoBackChannelError) still broken under pickling. #2478's _restore_mcp_error hardcodes a UrlElicitationRequiredError branch and reconstructs via from_error/from_error_data, which drops any instance state not represented in ErrorData and requires editing the dispatcher for each future special-cased subclass. #3262's test changes add NoBackChannelError to the pickle test imports, demonstrating the fix's generality across subclasses without custom reconstruction methods.

clusters.pick_reason: #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() before inspecting union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the common idiomatic pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None`. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() checks raw union args against a frozenset of bare types {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated-wrapped str member never matches the frozenset and _should_pre_parse_json still returns True - the corruption bug persists for any Optional[str] parameter that carries a Field/description via Annotated, which is a very common shape in practice. #3056's docstring also gives an explicit rationale for scoping the fix to str|None specifically (vs. e.g. str|list[str], where a member other than str could legitimately arise from JSON decoding), whereas #2032's broader 'skip for any union of scalar types' rule risks skipping legitimate int/float/bool coercion for unions like str|int or str|bool.

clusters.pick_reason: #3243 is the only one of the three that also addresses a correctness gap in the other two approaches: httpx can resume or close the async_auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that entered the `async with self.context.lock` block, which is unsafe with anyio.Lock's owner-task release semantics. #3243 replaces the single Lock with two task-agnostic anyio.Semaphore(1) locks (`lock` and `flow_lock`), separating token-acquisition serialization from the refresh/authorization transition. #3252's fix (move `yield request` outside the lock, re-acquire around the 401/403 branches) keeps the same Lock type and task-ownership assumption. #2858 is a rebase of an older, previously stalled PR (#2660); the diff available for it shows only import/docstring cleanup (the httpx2->httpx typo), not the actual lock-scope restructuring, so its concrete handling of the same-task-resumption issue is unverified.

members.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.

clusters.pick_reason: #3056 adds _unwrap_annotated() before inspecting union members, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the common idiomatic pattern `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None`. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() checks raw union args against a frozenset of bare types {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated-wrapped str member never matches the frozenset and _should_pre_parse_json still returns True - the corruption bug persists for any Optional[str] parameter that carries a Field/description via Annotated, which is a very common shape in practice. #3056's docstring also gives an explicit rationale for scoping the fix to str|None specifically (vs. e.g. str|list[str], where a member other than str could legitimately arise from JSON decoding), whereas #2032's broader 'skip for any union of scalar types' rule risks skipping legitimate int/float/bool coercion for unions like str|int or str|bool.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py only skipped JSON pre-parsing when a field's annotation was exactly `str`, so any union type containing `str` (e.g. `str | None`) still got run through json.loads(), silently corrupting string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. '{"a":1}' or 'null'). clusters.pick_reason: #2654 fixes the reported blocking bug by default (write buffer 0->1) with no API change, and adds a targeted regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces a handler queuing a response while a progress notification is still being flushed. #2215 instead adds two new public parameters (read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size) but leaves both defaults at 0, so out of the box it does not change behavior or fix the blocking scenario -- callers would have to know to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1 themselves. Both PRs edit the identical lines that construct read_stream/write_stream in stdio.py, so merging either first will conflict with the other; #2654's diff also targets a stream-construction helper (create_context_streams) that differs from #2215's (anyio.create_memory_object_stream), indicating the two branches are based on diverging versions of stdio.py and would need manual reconciliation regardless.

clusters.pick_reason: #3243 is the only one of the three that also addresses a correctness gap in the other two approaches: httpx can resume or close the async_auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that entered the `async with self.context.lock` block, which is unsafe with anyio.Lock's owner-task release semantics. #3243 replaces the single Lock with two task-agnostic anyio.Semaphore(1) locks (`lock` and `flow_lock`), separating token-acquisition serialization from the refresh/authorization transition. #3252's fix (move `yield request` outside the lock, re-acquire around the 401/403 branches) keeps the same Lock type and task-ownership assumption. #2858 is a rebase of an older, previously stalled PR (#2660); the diff available for it shows only import/docstring cleanup (the httpx2->httpx typo), not the actual lock-scope restructuring, so its concrete handling of the same-task-resumption issue is unverified.

members.cluster_pick_reason: #3243 is the only one of the three that also addresses a correctness gap in the other two approaches: httpx can resume or close the async_auth_flow generator from a different task than the one that entered the `async with self.context.lock` block, which is unsafe with anyio.Lock's owner-task release semantics. #3243 replaces the single Lock with two task-agnostic anyio.Semaphore(1) locks (`lock` and `flow_lock`), separating token-acquisition serialization from the refresh/authorization transition. #3252's fix (move `yield request` outside the lock, re-acquire around the 401/403 branches) keeps the same Lock type and task-ownership assumption. #2858 is a rebase of an older, previously stalled PR (#2660); the diff available for it shows only import/docstring cleanup (the httpx2->httpx typo), not the actual lock-scope restructuring, so its concrete handling of the same-task-resumption issue is unverified.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add rejection of an id already in flight, but #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids like int `1` and string "1" into the same key — a numeric id in flight would falsely reject a same-valued string id (or vice versa), and a string id equal to the literal "_GET_stream" could still collide with GET_STREAM_KEY. #3221 replaces this with a `_request_stream_key()` helper that prefixes by type (`i:`/`s:`), preserving the int/string distinction and structurally preventing collision with GET_STREAM_KEY, closing gaps #3063 leaves open while solving the same duplicate-id problem.
